message.content:
Repo: H:\Kasirku (Next.js 16 App Router POS/accounting SaaS "Kasirku"). I'm restricting the Android app (Capacitor-wrapped, in android-app/) so that no matter who logs in, it only ever shows a minimal "POS app" experience (Kasir/POS screen, Aktivitas/transaction history, Shift, limited Pengaturan) and NEVER the full owner backoffice dashboard (Dashboard/Laporan/Kelola Produk/Bahan Baku/Pelanggan/Kelola Kasir/Kelola Admin/etc, which showed up in a screenshot as a hamburger sidebar menu). The full backoffice should remain reachable normally from a regular desktop browser — this restriction should apply ONLY when running inside the native Android app.

I need factual answers, not recommendations yet:

1. `src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` — I've seen the top of this file (queries businesses, redirects to /onboarding if none). Show the REST of the file — specifically how each business card is rendered, especially any "Buka Kasir" button/link and any "Kelola" button/link. What exact URL does each go to (e.g. `/business/[id]/pos` vs `/business/[id]`)?

2. Find the component that renders the hamburger/sidebar menu with items like "Dashboard, Laporan, Riwayat Transaksi, Riwayat Shift, Kas Harian, Kelola Produk, Bahan Baku, Meja & Self-Order, Pelanggan, Kelola Kasir, Pengaturan, Kelola Admin" (likely named something like `DashboardShell` based on prior session context) — where is this file, what route(s)/layout render it, and how is it structured (is it a client component, does it read businessId from a prop or params, is there an existing mechanism for conditionally showing/hiding menu items e.g. based on permissions from `business_staff`/`src/lib/permissions.ts`)?

3. What's the exact URL path for `/business/[businessId]` root (no further segment) and `/business/[businessId]/pos` — are these two literally different route groups/layouts? Is `/business/[businessId]` (the "Kelola" destination) part of the `(dashboard)` route group I've seen referenced (e.g. `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/...`)? Show the layout.tsx for that `(dashboard)` route group if it exists, and for the `pos/` route (I already know `pos/layout.tsx` exists from prior context, but confirm what it renders/wraps).

4. Search for any EXISTING `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` usage in the codebase (I've added a few this session: dispatch-print-jobs.ts, add-printer-form.tsx) — list every file that currently imports `@capacitor/core`, so I know everywhere platform-detection is already wired in vs where I'd need to add it fresh.

5. `src/app/login/page.tsx`'s `handleSubmit` — confirm it does `router.push("/dashboard")` after successful login (already seen this, just confirm still current), and check if there's any other post-signup/post-auth redirect target I should know about (e.g. does `/onboarding` also eventually push to `/dashboard`, or does the whole app have a SINGLE place where "log in successfully" leads, or are there multiple entry points).

Report with file:line references — I'll design the actual restriction logic myself.

## 1. `src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` — rest of the file Full file: `H:\Kasirku\src\app\dashboard\page.tsx` (229 lines). The part after the redirect-to-onboarding guard maps over `businesses` and renders a card per business with two action links, at **lines 200–213**: ```tsx
🛎️ Buka Kasir Kelola →
``` - **"Buka Kasir"** → `/business/[id]/pos` (line 202) - **"Kelola"** → `/business/[id]` (line 208, no further segment — this resolves inside the `(dashboard)` route group) There's also a "Tambah Toko Baru" card linking to `/onboarding` (lines 218–224). ## 2. The sidebar/hamburger component File: `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\dashboard-shell.tsx` — exported default `DashboardShell` (line 385). - **Client component**: `"use client"` at line 1. - **Rendered by**: `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\layout.tsx` (the `(dashboard)` route-group layout), which is a server component that fetches the business, determines `isOwner`, loads `business_staff.permissions` for non-owners, and passes everything as props into `` (layout.tsx lines 52–66). So **`businessId` comes in as a prop from the layout**, not read directly from `params`/`useParams` inside the shell itself. - **Structure**: `buildNavGroups(businessId, businessType, isFinanceOnly)` (dashboard-shell.tsx line 59) builds 3 `NavGroup`s ("Utama", "Fitur Lanjutan", "Lainnya") containing all the items you listed (Dashboard line 77, Laporan line 85, Riwayat Transaksi line 86, Riwayat Shift line 88, Kas Harian line 91, Kelola Produk line 95, Bahan Baku line 98, Meja & Self-Order line 100–104, Pelanggan line 113, Kelola Kasir line 114, Pengaturan line 116, Kelola Admin line 117). Desktop sidebar is a fixed `
` (line 423); mobile is a hamburger button (line 462, "☰") that opens a drawer (`mobileNavOpen` state, lines 438–456). - **Existing permission mechanism already present**: yes. - `NavItem.ownerOnly` flag (dashboard-shell.tsx line 55) — set on "settings" (line 116) and "admins" (line 117), never shown to staff regardless of granted permissions. - `isItemAllowed(item, isOwner, permissions)` (lines 188–193): owner sees everything; `ownerOnly` items always hidden for non-owners; `dashboard` key always allowed; otherwise checked against `permissions.includes(item.key)`. - `filterGroupsForPermissions(groups, isOwner, permissions)` (lines 195–204) filters the nav groups before render (used at line 412: `const visibleGroups = filterGroupsForPermissions(...)`). - Permission keys/labels source of truth: `H:\Kasirku\src\lib\permissions.ts` (`PERMISSION_GROUPS`, `ALL_PERMISSION_KEYS`), explicitly documented as hand-kept-in-sync with the `key` values in `dashboard-shell.tsx`'s `buildNavGroups()` (permissions.ts lines 1–8). - Even when `isAllowed` is false for the active route, the shell still renders the sidebar chrome and just swaps `children` for an `` in main content (dashboard-shell.tsx lines 385, 418, 516) — i.e., the sidebar itself has no "hide entirely" mode currently, only per-item filtering. ## 3. Route structure: `/business/[businessId]` vs `/business/[businessId]/pos` Directory layout under `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\`: ``` (dashboard)/ ← route group, has layout.tsx (DashboardShell) billing/ ← no layout.tsx of its own (unwrapped, no shell) pos/ ← has layout.tsx (billing-lock check only) ``` There is **no** `layout.tsx` directly at `src/app/business/[businessId]/` root — so `(dashboard)` and `pos` are two independent layout trees, not nested under a shared parent layout. - `/business/[businessId]` (the "Kelola" link, no further segment) **is** served from `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/page.tsx`, i.e. it **is** part of the `(dashboard)` route group and gets wrapped in `DashboardShell` via `(dashboard)/layout.tsx`. `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` (full content, `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\layout.tsx`): ```tsx export default async function BusinessDashboardLayout({ children, params }: {...}) { const { businessId } = await params; const supabase = await createClient(); const [{ data: business }, { data: userData }, access] = await Promise.all([...]); if (!business) notFound(); const isOwner = business.owner_id === userData.user?.id; let permissions: string[] = []; if (!isOwner) { const { data: staff } = await supabase.from("business_staff")... if (!staff || !staff.active) notFound(); permissions = staff.permissions; } if (access.locked) redirect(`/business/${businessId}/billing`); return ( {children} ); } ``` This is the layout that applies to **every** route under `(dashboard)` — `dashboard` (root), `reports`, `transactions`, `products`, `ingredients`, `customers`, `cashiers`, `settings`, `admins`, `accounting/*`, etc. — all 27 subfolders listed in that directory get the full sidebar. `pos/layout.tsx` (full content, `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\pos\layout.tsx`, 22 lines): ```tsx export default async function PosLayout({ children, params }: {...}) { const { businessId } = await params; const supabase = await createClient(); const access = await getSubscriptionAccess(supabase, businessId); if (access.locked) redirect(`/business/${businessId}/billing`); return children; } ``` Confirmed: it does **not** render any shell/sidebar chrome at all — it only does a billing-lock check server-side and passes `children` straight through. The actual POS UI (Kasir screen) comes from `pos/page.tsx` plus `pos/pos-screen.tsx` / `pos/ticket-pos-screen.tsx` / `pos/open-shift-screen.tsx` / `pos/pin-screen.tsx` / `pos/member-panel.tsx` / `pos/switch-cashier-button.tsx`, with `pos/check-in/` and `pos/printers/` as sub-routes. `billing/` has `page.tsx`, `actions.ts`, `pay-button.tsx` but **no `layout.tsx`** — so it's unwrapped by any shell (no sidebar, no pos-layout billing-check, since its own page.tsx presumably handles its own display). ## 4. Existing `@capacitor/core` imports Files importing from `@capacitor/core`: - `H:\Kasirku\src\lib\dispatch-print-jobs.ts` — line 3: `import { Capacitor } from "@capacitor/core";`, used at line 15: `if (Capacitor.isNativePlatform()) {` - `H:\Kasirku\src\app\business\[businessId]\(dashboard)\settings\add-printer-form.tsx` — line 4: `import { Capacitor } from "@capacitor/core";`, used at line 27: `const isNative = Capacitor.isNativePlatform();` - `H:\Kasirku\src\lib\kitchen-printer-plugin.ts` — line 1: `import { registerPlugin } from "@capacitor/core";` (doesn't call `isNativePlatform()` itself — it just registers the native bridge plugin; a comment at line 4 references `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()` as what callers should check before invoking it). (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and the `android-app/` copies are just the dependency manifest entries, not source usage.)
